claim: Raw, unfiltered 1kHz LFP in V198o and V182o sessions shows periodic, large-amplitude, broadband deflections that are synchronous across essentially all 128 channels of a probe simultaneously -- the textbook signature of a movement/electrode artifact, not neural signal (genuine LFP varies by depth/area and would not produce an identical instantaneous kink on every channel at once). A same-method C31o session does not show this signature: its LFP is broadband-noisier overall (max ~150 uV) but has no isolated, order-of-magnitude spikes standing above baseline the way V198o/V182o do.
evidence: scripts/check_lfp_movement_artifacts.py (new script, reuses resolve_lfp_datasets/bytes-safe trial-table coercion from extract_lfp_coupling_matrices.py / precompute_tfr_arrays.py)
outputs/qc_lfp_artifacts/V198o_230714_probe_0_lfp_zoom.png -- sharp synchronous all-channel deflections at ~t=9s, ~t=11-12s within a 25s window
outputs/qc_lfp_artifacts/V182o_260629_probe_0_lfp_zoom.png -- same signature at ~t=1s, ~5.5s, plus an all-channel-synchronous oscillatory burst ~15.5-16.5s

outputs/qc_lfp_artifacts/{V198o_230714,V182o_260629,C31o_230823_control}_probe_0_lfp_popmean.png -- cross-channel mean |LFP| quantifies the effect: V198o baseline ~50-100 uV punctuated by spikes to 600-700 uV (6-12x); V182o baseline ~20-30 uV punctuated by spikes to ~300 uV (10-15x); C31o control tops out ~150 uV with no comparable isolated spike
raw amplitude range over the same 20-correct-trial window: V198o [-905, +1039] uV; V182o [-365, +190] uV; C31o control [-272, +312] uV
notes: Method: 20 consecutive correct trials (stimulus_number==2, correct==1, any condition, time-sorted -- NOT restricted to RRRR) pulled from the real trial sequence starting 1/3 of the way into each session (to avoid recording-start/end edge effects), all 128 channels of probe_0, completely unfiltered raw LFP as stored in the NWB acquisition group. Checked visually (not just amplitude stats) by rendering the full stack and a zoomed window around the largest pop-mean spike.

Removal strategy evaluated 2026-08-06: (1) common-mode synchrony detector (per-channel robust z via median/MAD, then median |z| across channels per timepoint) -- clean separation, sparse (0.02-0.04% of samples flagged at z>8 threshold). (2) Common-median referencing (subtract per-timepoint cross-channel median) tested on the V198o reference window: synchrony-z dropped 9.4->4.2, peak amplitude range shrank ~45-55% but artifact was NOT eliminated -- CMR alone is insufficient, artifact is not perfectly uniform in amplitude across all 128 channels. (3) A per-channel temporal median filter was evaluated and rejected as the wrong tool -- it doesn't exploit the artifact's spatial (cross-channel) structure, and a window wide enough to suppress it would also distort genuine gamma-band signal (12-33ms cycles) the project's headline result depends on. RECOMMENDATION: detect via the synchrony statistic, reject contaminated trials (same pattern as this project's existing quality/trial_presence_fraction gates), not filter.

Full-session contamination rate (probe_0 only, whole recording, not just the 20-trial reference window): V198o_230714 -- 3,347/16,432,086 samples flagged (0.0204%), 33/960 correct trials (3.44%) have their -1000..+3990ms p1-relative analysis window overlap a flagged sample. V182o_260629 -- 5,781/15,556,054 samples flagged (0.0372%), 75/961 correct trials (7.80%) contaminated. Rejection at these rates is cheap relative to typical ephys QC losses. NOT YET CHECKED: other probes in the same sessions (V198o has probe_1; V182o has probes 1-3) -- if the artifact is genuinely session-wide/mechanical it should appear on all probes at the same timestamps, and the true per-session rejection rate (if requiring all probes clean) could be higher than the probe_0-only number above.

2026-08-06, session-wise multi-probe detection (scripts/repair_lfp_movement_artifacts.py): per user direction, repair (linear interpolation over detected intervals) replaces rejection, and detection was run per-session across all of a session's probes at once (all probes share an identical sample clock -- verified, same n_samples/ts[0]/ts[-1] on every probe of both sessions). V198o: 187 session-level (union) intervals, 162 seen on only 1 of 2 probes, 25 on both. V182o: 441 union intervals, 382 on only 1 of 4 probes, 40 on 2, 18 on 3, 1 on all 4. IMPORTANT CORRECTION caught before shipping a repair: directly inspected the 302 probe_0-only V182o events (of 382 single-probe total) and found the OTHER THREE PROBES SIT AT BACKGROUND z (median ~2-3, max 75th percentile ~5, well under the z=8 threshold) at those exact timestamps -- these are genuinely probe_0-LOCAL events, not a session-wide artifact merely sub-threshold elsewhere. This means repair must use each probe's OWN detected intervals, not the cross-probe union -- an earlier version of the script would have interpolated real, uncontaminated signal on probes 1-3 at probe_0-only event times. Fixed. The smaller multi-probe-corroborated set (59 events for V182o: n=2,3,4) shows a clean, consistent monotonic amplitude gradient (probe_0 > probe_1 > probe_2 > probe_3 in peak z, every single time) -- this pattern IS consistent with a genuine shared physical event whose coupling strength attenuates smoothly by probe, unlike the probe_0-only population. Two distinct populations, not one: a small genuinely-shared-artifact set, and a much larger probe_0-specific-noise set (cause not established -- could still be movement with probe_0 uniquely susceptible via its own cabling/mounting, or an unrelated probe_0-local electrical issue; not distinguishable from LFP shape alone).

TFR/spectrogram confirmation (2026-08-06): a sharp time-domain impulse is, by Fourier duality, flat/broadband in the frequency domain -- exactly what a raw (non-baseline-normalized) spectrogram shows at these artifact instants. Verified quantitatively on V198o probe_0 ch60: before-vs-after-repair spectrogram difference is 99-100% of tested frequencies (0-150Hz) elevated >3dB at the two detected instants (mean 20-26dB removed), and EXACTLY 0.00dB everywhere else checked -- a clean, well-controlled confirmation (paired same-signal comparison, not a hand-picked 'clean' reference point, which was tried first and was too confounded by natural 1/f drift to be convincing). This directly explains why some existing TFR/spectrogram figures in this project show a flat, all-frequency vertical line at certain timepoints -- that line is this artifact, not a real broadband power event.

Threshold lowered z>8 -> z>6 per user direction (2026-08-06), synchrony-z arrays now CACHED to outputs/lfp_artifact_repair/<session>_<probe>_synchrony_z.npy so future threshold changes are near-instant (no ~200s/probe rescan needed). New counts: V198o probe_0/1 = 193/172 (was 95/118), V182o probe_0/1/2/3 = 922/443/192/288 (was 366/85/44/30). Corroboration improved too: V182o now has 12 events seen on all 4 probes (was 1).

CRITICAL CONFOUND FOUND AND FIXED: reward is delivered at an essentially fixed latency post-p1 across trials (measured directly from the reward_1_tracking acquisition channel, not assumed -- V182o 4139-4142ms, <4ms jitter across 26 trials; V198o 4120-4138ms, <20ms jitter across 15 trials). A histogram of z>6 detected-interval timing relative to the nearest preceding trial onset showed a sharp spike at exactly this latency (38 events in the 4000-4200ms bin alone, vs 4-18 in every other 200ms bin) -- i.e. lowering the threshold started catching reward-locked events, which the user explicitly separated from 'movement artifact in correct trials' and does not want conflated with this repair. Fixed by adding reward_adjacent_mask() to repair_lfp_movement_artifacts.py: excludes any sample within [4000,4300]ms of ANY correct trial's p1 onset (session-wide, all conditions, not just AAAB) from repair eligibility, writing the excluded events to a separate <session>_<probe>_reward_excluded.csv rather than silently dropping them. Effect: V198o probe_0/1 reward-excluded counts = 2/65 (barely changes probe_0's already-low count, removes a real chunk of probe_1's); V182o probe_0/1/2/3 = 42/26/5/0.

AAAB trial-averaged raw-LFP before/after repair (2026-08-06, scripts/check_lfp_movement_artifacts.py::aaab_trial_average_before_after), reward window excluded: V198o probe_0, 221 correct AAAB trials, only 6 (2.7%) touched by any repair interval, max abs change in the trial average = 5.78uV vs a raw trial-average dynamic range of [-311,469]uV (~1.2%) -- the AAAB evoked response (clear stimulus-locked deflections at p1/p2/p3/p4) is visually identical before/after, as expected given how few trials are affected. V182o probe_0, 214 trials, 41 (19.2%, down from 52/24.3% before the reward fix) touched, max abs change = 4.59uV vs range [-37,14]uV (~9%) -- non-negligible for this probe specifically. The before/after difference trace initially looked suspiciously smooth/continuous rather than sparse, which raised a real concern (checked, not assumed) -- direct verification showed 71.9% of the 4200ms trial window is touched by AT LEAST ONE of the 214 trials' own repair interval (max 4 trials overlapping at any single timepoint), which is the expected, legitimate aggregate signature of a high per-trial event rate (~900 detected events across ~960 correct trials on V182o probe_0, i.e. roughly 1 per trial on average) landing at different random within-trial times across different trials -- NOT a bug, and not solely the (already-excluded) reward cluster.

Non-trial-locked signal-quality check (2026-08-06, aaab_single_trial_quality_before_after), added because trial-averaging is blind by construction to non-phase-locked contamination (a random-timing event in a minority of trials contributes ~1/n to the mean and mostly washes out). Two metrics that do NOT wash out: (1) cross-trial SD as a function of within-trial time -- V182o probe_0 shows the after-repair (red) line sitting below before-repair (black) at essentially every transient spike across the whole trial window (e.g. ~1100, 1500, 1700, 2500, 3000, 3650ms), a clean direct demonstration of reduced non-repeatable trial-to-trial variability; V198o probe_0 shows a much smaller effect (few visible gaps between the two lines), consistent with its much lower contamination rate (6/221 vs 41/214 trials). (2) per-trial peak|LFP| across all channels, pooled (not averaged) across trials -- V182o's before-repair distribution has a long right tail out past 600uV that collapses almost entirely after repair; V198o shows only 2 outlier trials removed, matching its low contamination rate. Both sessions show ONE persistent, UNCHANGED spike at ~4150-4200ms surviving in both before AND after -- this is the reward-onset transient (correctly, deliberately excluded from repair by reward_adjacent_mask, not a detector failure) and its persistence in both plots is a useful internal consistency check that the exclusion is behaving as intended. Aggregate/pooled stats across ALL trials are diluted by the majority of untouched trials (V198o mean cross-trial SD reduced only 1.3%, V182o only 3.5%) -- the real, larger effect is concentrated in the minority of contaminated trials, which the two plots above show directly; V198o's single worst trial peak dropped from 1388.5uV to 803.5uV.

SECOND, DIFFERENT detector built 2026-08-06 per explicit direction (scripts/check_lfp_movement_artifacts.py::cross_trial_median_repair): 'outliers found as non-time-trial-locked single spikes, removed via between-trial median interpolation', restricted to a 'fair window' of -500..+4000ms (excludes the reward-onset transient at ~4120-4142ms, which would otherwise skew the outlier-magnitude distribution with a different, already-identified phenomenon). Compares each trial's value at a given (channel, within-trial-time) against the cross-trial median/MAD at that exact cell -- complementary to the earlier cross-CHANNEL-synchrony detector (which catches events synchronous across channels within one trial; this catches events that do not recur across trials at the same latency, independent of channel count).

Two real problems found and fixed before trusting this detector's output (both caught by checking, not assumed): (1) THRESHOLD DID NOT TRANSFER -- borrowing z>6 from the cross-channel detector overflagged massively: 405,629/127,296,000 cells (0.32%) but spread across so many (trial,channel) combinations that it touched 97.7% of V198o's 221 trials (13,616 flagged spike-intervals). The |z| distribution here is heavy-tailed (99.9th pctile=8.3, 99.99th=13.8, 99.999th=21.1), nothing like Gaussian z=6's expected ~2e-9 false-positive rate -- a different statistic needs its own calibration, not a borrowed number. (2) PER-INSTANT MAD MASKED THE WORST EVENT -- even at z>15/20/25 the pooled per-trial peak|LFP| metric was COMPLETELY UNCHANGED (before==after exactly) for V198o. Traced directly: the single largest event in the dataset (channel 88, 1388.5uV, 3.3x that channel's own median) was flagged in ZERO trials at z>15. Cause: MAD computed per-(timepoint,channel) is itself inflated at timepoints where trials naturally vary a lot (e.g. during an evoked response), which masks a genuinely huge deviation by measuring it against an already-large local scale -- backwards from what's wanted. FIX: MAD computed per-CHANNEL ONLY, pooled across all trials AND all timepoints in the window (n = n_trials*n_win, much more stable, does not adapt to local variance by design). After the fix, channel 88's event scores z=20.97, cleanly separated from the next-highest (12.1) -- a natural threshold gap.

FINAL, validated cross-trial-median result (z>15, per-channel-pooled MAD, fair window, reward-adjacent-window not separately needed here since the window itself excludes it): V198o probe_0, 221 trials, 293 (trial,channel) spikes flagged across 5 trials (2.3%) -- peak|LFP| max 1388.5uV -> 1021.6uV, p99 802.8 -> 798.1uV (small effect, matches this probe's already-low contamination). V182o probe_0, 214 trials, 661 spikes across 25 trials (11.7%) -- peak|LFP| max 791.5 -> 631.0uV, p99 594.5 -> 484.6uV (real, visible tail reduction). Repair method: crossfade from actual trial signal into the cross-trial median trace across CROSS_TRIAL_PAD_MS=20ms at each edge of a flagged span, stay at the median through the flagged core, crossfade back out -- avoids a discontinuity jump at either boundary, per explicit direction ('between trial median interpolation only for the spike').

Multi-condition validation (2026-08-06, multi_condition_noise_reduction_grid), per explicit direction to check AAAB/RRRR/BBBA together, each condition's cross-trial median/MAD computed SEPARATELY (pooling conditions would blur the trial-locked evoked shape, which differs by condition -- RRRR has no consistent deviant position, AAAB/BBBA do). Confirms the method generalizes, not an AAAB-specific artifact of the analysis: V182o probe_0 -- AAAB 25/214 trials touched (11.7%), peak max 792->631uV; RRRR 26/120 (21.7%), peak max 2508->901uV (largest single reduction found in this whole investigation, p99 2451->638uV); BBBA 38/213 (17.8%), peak max 1610->1127uV, p99 1498->521uV. V198o probe_0 -- consistently smaller effect across all three conditions (touched 1.9-7.1%, mean cross-trial SD reduction 0.5-2.6%), matching its already-established lower contamination rate relative to V182o. NOTE: an early run of this grid accidentally used the module default z_thresh=6.0 instead of the validated z_thresh=15 (touched 88-98% of trials, same overflagging failure mode already diagnosed and fixed) -- caught before reporting, corrected by passing z_thresh=15 explicitly; z_thresh does not have a safe default value for this function and must be passed.

Only probe_0 checked per session so far -- V198o has a second probe (probe_1_lfp) and V182o has three more (probe_1/2/3_lfp) not yet checked; if the artifact is genuinely mechanical/movement-driven it should appear on every probe in the same session at the same timestamps, which would be a stronger confirmatory receipt than a single-probe check.

This confirms the OBSERVATION (synchronous broadband impulses exist, disproportionately/exclusively in V198o and V182o relative to a C31o control) but does NOT yet confirm the MECHANISM (movement specifically, as opposed to e.g. an electrical/grounding artifact) -- both sessions' NWB files also carry eye_1_tracking/pupil_1_tracking acquisition streams; cross-referencing spike timestamps against those would be the natural next receipt if the user wants the movement attribution nailed down rather than inferred from the artifact's shape alone.

Downstream implication not yet acted on: every LFP-based figure/analysis in this project (fig04/05/06 LFP-LFP, fig07 spike-LFP coupling, all TFR/band-power pipelines) pools across sessions including these two subjects. If these impulses survive into the band-power/TFR pipeline without rejection, they could inflate variance or bias baseline-normalized dB values in specific sessions -- worth checking whether trial-level outlier rejection already catches this before treating it as a live risk to existing results.
